subject: Math
prompt:
$$4(3x) + 11(2y) = 77$$

$$4(3x) - 11(2y) = -77$$

The solution to the given system of equations is $(x, y)$. What is the value of $3x + 2y$?
explanation: Choice B is correct. Adding the two given equations eliminates the $11(2y)$ terms: $[4(3x) + 11(2y)] + [4(3x) - 11(2y)] = 77 + (-77)$, which simplifies to $8(3x) = 0$, so $3x = 0$. Subtracting the second equation from the first gives $[4(3x) + 11(2y)] - [4(3x) - 11(2y)] = 77 - (-77)$, which simplifies to $22(2y) = 154$, so $2y = 7$. Therefore, $3x + 2y = 0 + 7 = 7$.
